title: A1-16 · House and city; the denial withلَيْسَ‎

blocks.text: A1-16 · House and city; the denial with ⁧لَيْسَ⁩
Lesson overview

The house is not large ,   , I am not Egyptian , , there is the elevator , to deny a nominal phrase the Arabic uses ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ , a word that combines like a verb and that puts the predicate to the accusative: . ⁧البَيْتُ لَيْسَ كَبِيرًا⁩ In this unit you learn it along with the vocabulary of the house and neighborhood, read real estate ads and describe the place where you live. Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 38–39 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-16), vocal synthesis script, a plant of your home, session with the tutor in the second week
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. deny a nominal sentence with ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ and place the predicate on the accusative;
2. conjugate ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ with all singular and plural pronouns;
3. choose between ⁧لَا⁩ (verb) and ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ (rated sentence);
4. use ⁧غَيْر⁩ to deny an adjective ( ⁧غَيْرُ مَفْرُوشَةٍ⁩ );
5. read a rental announcement and ask an agency for information;
6. describe your home and neighborhood in 70 words.
Two-week plan.

1. : ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ deny the nominal sentence
Three rules.
1. The predicate goes to the accusative: ⁧كَبِيرٌ⁩ → ⁧كَبِيرًا⁩ , ⁧مَفْرُوشَةٌ⁩ → ⁧مَفْرُوشَةً⁩ . It is the only change in form of
sentence.
2. If the predicate is a complement with preposition or adverb ( ⁧فِي البَيْتِ⁩ , ⁧هُنَا⁩ ) nothing changes: the
Preposition already holds his case.
3. ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ agrees with the subject: ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ for a male subject, ⁧لَيْسَتْ⁩ for a female, ⁧لَسْتُ⁩ for .

The subject pronoun generally fails, because ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ it contains: ⁧لَسْتُ مِصْرِيًّا⁩ I'm not Egyptian. Because the accused. ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ is originally a verb (to not be) of the same family as ⁧كَانَ⁩ • to be: (A2): These verbs leave the subject to the name and put the predicate to the accusative. You'll find it in A1-19. In texts without vowels the predicate to the accusative can only be seen when there is the aliif of tanwīn: . ⁧البيت ليس كبيرا⁩ It's a good clue to recognize a nominal negation.
2. There's no squirrel and I don't have any
In the sentences ... there is / there are (A1-04) the subject comes after the complement and remains at the name:

rows: There's no elevator in the building.

blocks.text: . ⁧لَيْسَ عِنْدِي سَيَّارَةٌ⁩ laysa ʿindī sayyāra. I don't have a car. Here ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ it always remains to the singular male, whatever the subject: it is a fixed form, as in A1-08.
3. The conjugation of ⁧لَيْسَ⁩
⁧لَيْسَ⁩ it combines with the desinences of the perfect (which you will study in A1-18). When desinence begins by consonant, the root shortens in ⁧لَسْ⁩ -.
The two of them (f.) ⁧لَيْسَتَا⁩ laysatā

The most frequent are ⁧لَسْتُ⁩ , ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ , ⁧لَيْسَتْ⁩ , ⁧لَسْنَا⁩ , ⁧لَيْسُوا⁩ : learn them first. Note the accusative of plural predicate: ⁧مُهَنْدِسِينَ⁩ ( -īna), ⁧طُلَّابًا⁩ , and for the female plural -ātin: . ⁧لَسْنَ مُهَنْدِسَاتٍ⁩ Before the Article ⁧لَيْسَتْ⁩ Takes one of the support: ⁧لَيْسَتِ الشَّقَّةُ كَبِيرَةً⁩ laysati š-šaqqatu kabīra .

rows: . ⁧لَا أَسْكُنُ هُنَا⁩ I don't live here.
. ⁧لَسْتُ مِنْ هُنَا⁩ I'm not from here.

blocks.text: Always ask yourself: is there a verb? If so, ⁧لَا⁩ ; if not, ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ . Errors such as ⁧لا أنا مصري⁩ » o « ⁧ليس أعرف⁩ They are the most frequent at this level.
5. : ⁧غَيْر⁩ deny an adjective

⁧غَيْر⁩ "non-', other than followed by a name or adjective to the genitive forms the opposite: ⁧غَيْرُ مَفْرُوشٍ⁩ Not furnished, ⁧غَيْرُ صَحِيحٍ⁩ Incorrect, ⁧غَيْرُ مُمْكِنٍ⁩ "Impossible" ⁧غَيْرُ قَانُونِيٍّ⁩ Illegal. It is very common in the language of media and documents.
⁧هِجْرَةٌ غَيْرُ قَانُونِيَّةٍ⁩ hiǧratun ġayru qānūniyya irregular immigration

How it works out. ⁧غَيْر⁩ takes the case of the position (here named, predicate), the adjective that follows is always to the genitive and generally agrees with the name: . ⁧الشَّقَّةُ غَيْرُ مَفْرُوشَةٍ⁩

7. Pronunciation

⁧لَيْسَ⁩ and ⁧لَسْتُ⁩ . Laysa with the diphthong ay; lastu , lasnā I'll be there shortly. Don't say laystu. ⁧شَقَّة⁩ , ⁧حَمَّام⁩ , ⁧مَطْبَخ⁩ . šaqqa (q double, emphatic and uvular), ḥammām (ḥ faringale + double m), maṭbaḫ (ṭ stress + ḫ Final). The Accusative-an on pause. In the didactic examples we pronounce it: laysa kabīran ; in a classic break, you would say kabīrā . Many say laysa in the quick reading kabīr : Admit it. . ⁧مِصْعَد⁩ miṣʿad : ṣād emphasis followed by ʿayn.
